invoking: by what means might the mandala be unsealed?

kernel.governing_law: The scroll is unsealed not by one who conquers and grasps it, but by the hidden surrender of the one who holds it — shadow-power yields, it is not seized.
kernel.mutated_relation: In 5:7, the direction of agency flips: the Lamb approaching and taking FROM the enthroned one becomes the enthroned one releasing and extending TOWARD the Lamb — the throne is the active origin of transfer, not the passive source.

clause_map.note: Seals reread as thresholds held by the throne's right hand, not locks placed on the scroll's exterior.
Proclamation reframed: not 'who is worthy to take?' but 'to whom may it be given?' — receiver-worthiness replaced by throne-permission.
Inability recast: no one could be found to whom it could be released, not merely no one able to seize it.
Weeping shifts cause: grief is for absence of one the throne will release toward, not absence of a capable taker.
Lion/Root victory is the condition that compels the throne's open hand, not a credential authorising a grasp.
The Lamb's nature and the seven spirits are structural constants — their description does not depend on direction of transfer.
Core flip: throne-agent extends/releases scroll outward toward Lamb; Lamb receives rather than takes — agency and arrow reversed.

artifacts.enantiomorph:
**5:1** I saw, upon the throne a hand holding a scroll written within and on the back, sealed with seven seals, and the door was shut fast.

**5:2** I saw a mighty angel crying out with a great voice: Who is worthy to receive the prize — to open the scroll from the throne and loose its seven seals?

**5:3** None was found — neither in the heavens above, nor across the earth, nor beneath it — who could open the scroll from the throne.

**5:4** I wept bitterly, for no one was found worthy to take the scroll into their hands.

**5:5** Then one of the elders said to me: Weep no more — the Lion of the sword and the victory, the branch and root of the ancient seat, has prevailed to take the scroll and open its seven seals.

**5:6** And I saw in the midst of the throne and the four living creatures and in the midst of the elders a Lamb standing as though slain, having seven horns and seven eyes, which are the seven spirits of God sent out into all the earth.

**5:7** And he came and took the scroll from the right hand of the one seated upon the throne.

independent.recovered_law: In TEXT A the scroll is in the right hand of the one seated on the throne (and the Lamb takes it from that right hand); in TEXT B the scroll is upon/of the throne itself (a hand upon the throne holds it), reattributing possession from the enthroned figure's right hand to the throne as the locus, until verse 5:7 reverts to the Lamb taking it from the right hand of the one seated on the throne.
independent.law_match_note: The recovered claim identifies a real structural change—relocation of scroll possession from the enthroned one's right hand to the throne as locus—but frames it as a possession/attribution shift, not an agency-direction flip where the throne becomes the active origin of transfer toward the Lamb.
independent.terminal_note: Verse 5:7 of TEXT B explicitly reverts to TEXT A's structure — the Lamb takes the scroll from the right hand of the one seated on the throne — abandoning the throne-as-holder relation established in 5:1–5:5.
